sections.body: Every saint icon now carries a record of where it came from.

sections.heading: These notes fold into years and months
sections.body: These notes fold into years and months, so 89 releases are no longer one flat column.

sections.heading: The opening offer is withdrawn
sections.body: Both paid tiers were advertised at half off the first year and the discount never actually applied at checkout, so the claim is gone from the pricing pages, the plan copy and the Terms rather than left standing. Nobody was charged a discounted rate that later rose; the prices shown have always been the prices charged.

title: Purify on iPhone
intro: Purify has been an Android app and a website. It is an iPhone app as well now, built from the same library and working the same way with no signal, and that is most of this release. The rest is a short run of repairs. One of them took the navigation away for as long as the anthem was playing. One is a single word in the Psalter that has been wrong since it was transcribed. And one is the half of a fix from four days ago that had been left undone, so that accounts made inside the app were shown the Terms and then kept no record of it. Beta 3.0 was finished on the second of August and held back so that it and the iPhone app could arrive together, so everything in its notes arrives with this.

sections.heading: Purify has an iPhone app
sections.body: There has been an iOS folder in Purify since the middle of June. What was in it would not have built, and had it built it would have been the wrong app: a window onto the website rather than Purify itself, which is neither what the Android app is nor something Apple accepts. It is a real app now, made from the same library and working the same way. The prayers, the Scriptures, the saints, the councils, the calendar and the whole reading room travel with it and open with no signal, exactly as on Android. As this goes out it is with Apple rather than on the App Store. Every app and every update is reviewed, and there is no honest way to name the day it will appear, so this note will not pretend to. One thing an iPhone reader should know in advance: swiping from the left edge to go back does nothing yet. Android's own back button has been handled for a long time and the iPhone gesture has not, and it is the first thing on the list after this.

sections.heading: Starting the anthem took the navigation away
sections.body: The player and the row of tabs were both pinned to the bottom of the screen, and the player was drawn on top of it. So beginning the anthem covered the navigation completely, and it stayed covered for as long as the music played: the only way to leave the screen you were on was to stop praying along. It was reported from a device, with a screenshot. The note in the code said the player sat above the tab bar so it would never be covered, which was an answer to the wrong question. Deciding which of two things paints on top does not stop them standing in the same place. The player now sits above the bar by exactly the bar's own height, measured from the same value the rest of the app uses for it, so the two cannot drift apart. On the website, where there is no tab bar, it stays at the bottom where it belongs.

sections.heading: The sheet on a verse was three faults, and only one of them showed
sections.body: Reported from a device as popups having no animation. It did not animate, and looking into that turned up two worse things in the same forty lines. It never told the tab bar to step aside, and it was drawn at the same depth as that bar while being rendered in place rather than lifted out to the top of the page, which means its depth was measured against the wrong thing entirely. Together those left the tab bar lit and, worse, still tappable over an open panel. That is the same shape as a fault reported twice from the Android beta, which cost a release to find the first time. Purify already had a component that had solved all three, with seven screens using it, so the verse panel now uses it too. Two further faults of the same kind were fixed while there: one panel raised the flag that moves the tab bar and never lowered it if it was closed by its parent, which left the tab bar dead for the rest of the session, and two others lowered it at the start of their closing animation, so the bar came back a fifth of a second before the panel had gone. This one has not been opened on a device yet, which is the only reason it is described here rather than declared fixed.

sections.heading: Six titles in the reading room were set in the wrong face
sections.body: They were rendering in DM Serif Display, which the app keeps for large ornate headings, at nineteen pixels in a list. That face draws its thin strokes very thin on purpose, and at list size they go spindly, so the titles read worse than the face the rest of the app reads in. They were paragraphs rather than headings, which is exactly how they slipped past the rule that puts every real heading in the right face. The page's own title keeps the display face, because at that size it is the ornate heading the face was added for.

sections.heading: Psalm 135:4 said along where it should say alone
sections.body: To him who along has wrought great wonders. Brenton reads alone, which is what the Greek says. A single transcription slip, and the whole psalter was checked to be sure it was the only one. It was. It came to light while confirming something worth writing down: Purify's Psalm 135 is the Polyeleos, Give thanks to the Lord for he is good, with its twenty-six fold refrain. A psalter of one hundred and fifty-one psalms is numbered the Septuagint way, so this is not the Psalm 135 of a King James Bible, and anything matched to Purify by that number needs to know which of the two it means.

sections.heading: Sign in with Apple works
sections.body: The sign-in screen has carried a greyed-out Apple button labelled coming soon since it was built, and the connected-accounts screen said coming soon even to readers whose account was already linked through Apple. Both of those are gone, replaced by the real thing rather than by a better promise. It is offered on the website, and it will be there on the iPhone app when that arrives. It is not offered in the Android app: Apple gives no proper way to do it there, and a button that fails after you have committed to it is worse than no button. The connected-accounts screen tells the truth now too, so an account already linked through Apple is described as connected.

sections.heading: Accounts made inside the app left no record of agreeing to the Terms
sections.body: Beta 3.0 said that five hundred and seventy-two accounts made through Google had never been shown the Terms, and fixed it. The fix was only half a fix, and this is the other half. The part that records the agreement runs on the website, at the moment the account comes back from Google. In the app nothing comes back from anywhere: it asks Google directly and is answered directly, so that moment never happens and nothing was written down. Everyone was shown the notice, which is the part that matters most, but the app kept no record of having shown it. It records one now, before it moves you on, and it does not repeat one for the same person. This depends on a change to the database that has to be applied by hand, so until that is done the record is still not being kept, and it should not be assumed to be.

sections.heading: Housekeeping, and what is still not on
sections.body: The iPhone app carries the same launcher cross as Android; the one in the project was still a stock placeholder from the day it was created, on a white background that would have flashed white every time the app opened. The check that holds Purify's version numbers in step now covers the iPhone one as well, which is the actual reason it sat at 1.0 for the whole of the Beta 2 series: it was in nobody's list. Two things are still dark and are not claimed here. Prayer reminders still cannot be delivered, for the reason given at length in the Beta 3.0 notes, and that has not changed. And Purify Plus is not purchasable on iPhone in this build; where it cannot be bought, the app says so plainly rather than offering a button that fails. Beta 3.0 was finished on the second of August and held so that it and the iPhone app could arrive together, so everything in its notes arrives with this one.

title: What the app was not saying
intro: Nearly everything here is something Purify already knew and was not telling you. The account of the Council of Florence was four paragraphs on the council the Orthodox reading of church history keeps returning to. A Father's page did not say when the words on it were not his. August could name six of its sixty-two commemorations. The daily page on a computer showed less of the day than the phone does, and its date read in English whatever language you had chosen. Accounts created through Google were shown no Terms at all, five hundred and seventy-two of them. The Android app had never reported a single session, and the prayer reminders had nothing scheduled to send them. This release is mostly the app saying what it already had.

sections.heading: The Council of Florence, at full length, and a new kind of section under it
sections.body: Florence was the thinnest account in the timeline, four paragraphs and three sources with no artwork, on the council the Orthodox reading of church history keeps returning to. It is about seven times longer now, sixteen paragraphs against four: the run up that everyone at the council remembered, the two questions actually put, whether the addition to the Creed was lawful and whether it was true, the wearing down of a delegation living on a papal allowance, and the decree of 5 July 1439 that thirty-three Greeks signed and Mark of Ephesus did not. There is a section on what flowed from it, from Varna to the synod of 1484 that set the union aside, and a note saying plainly which parts of the story are contested. Sources go from three to nine, four of them modern histories, one of which is sympathetic to the union. Under the narrative sits something new to the format rather than to this one article: a step by step timeline, twenty-four dated steps from 1274 to 1484 with its seven turning points drawn heavier. Any long event can carry one now, and Florence is the first to use it. It is a numbered list underneath, so it reads in order to a screen reader, and a check refuses any timeline whose steps lack a date, lack a claim, or run backwards. Four images arrive with it, shown in Immersive History, each with its source and licence recorded: Pisanello's sketches of the emperor made at the council itself, the decree with its Latin and Greek columns and its two seals, a Gozzoli fresco, and a Nuremberg Chronicle woodcut. Florence sits higher on the timeline now and answers to two more names in search, Laetentur Caeli and the Union of 1439. And five studies in the theology library, among them the one on why the Church does not receive Florence, now carry a link to the events behind them.

sections.heading: Saints' pages say whose words you are reading
sections.body: A Father's page is set in serif, and a reader skimming it is entitled to assume the serif is the Father speaking. On a number of works that assumption was wrong, and nothing on the page said so except a sentence at the end of a long editor's note. The Martyrdom of Polycarp is the church of Smyrna writing about him. St Nicholas's troparion is the Church's hymn to him. The miracles in the Life of Antony are Athanasius narrating. Each of those sections now carries a quiet band above it naming whose words follow, set in sans against the reading serif so a skimmer registers it without being shouted at. Where the words are the saint's own, which is the usual case, it says nothing at all. One hundred and thirty-three sections across fifty-three works are labelled so far, fewer than one in ten of the library, and the rest are left unlabelled rather than guessed at. The same restraint now governs what search engines and machine readers are told: a work carrying our own retelling is no longer published as a book the saint wrote, and a work whose sections are not yet labelled makes no claim about its author at all. That is the one class of mistake nothing ever corrects, because it is copied and repeated.

sections.heading: August has its saints
sections.body: The whole month, in two passes: thirty-seven new profiles, eleven for the first part of August and twenty-six after it. The month can now name forty-eight of its sixty-two commemorations, against six before this release. Stephen the Protomartyr, the first martyr of the Church, had no profile at all, and the second of August pointed nowhere. Two feasts that existed in the registry but had no place in the month are in it now, Irene the Empress on the seventh and Cosmas of Aetolia on the twenty-fourth. Where a public domain text exists the saint arrives with their own writings to read in full, one hundred and twenty-eight chapters and about thirty-one thousand five hundred words of them. Cyprian of Carthage comes with four: The Life and Passion of Cyprian, written by his own deacon Pontius, On the Unity of the Church, On the Lord's Prayer, and On the Mortality. The Abgar documents come with Thaddeus of Edessa. Six commemorations were held back rather than written thin, and the reason for each is written down. The tool that fetches and prepares these texts is new, and three faults in it were caught by the run itself, one of them visible to a reader: files that landed before the fix ended with a stray footnotes heading sitting inside a Father's text as though he had said it.

sections.heading: Today, on a computer
sections.body: On the web there is no Today tab. The daily prayer page is the only Today the site has, and it had been showing less of the day than the phone does, laid out for a narrow column. It now opens with the date and the day's fast set against it, then the one rule the hour asks for with a button to begin, then the Verse of the Day, which the web did not carry at all. Beside them, in their own column, is the Church's own reckoning of the day: the saint with their icon, the fast in full words, the appointed readings, and the count to Pascha. Those are drawn by the same part of the app the phone uses, so the two can no longer disagree about what day it is. The page holds more and is close to a third shorter, from about 2,500 pixels tall to about 1,800 on a 1440 by 900 screen, and the first screenful carries the date, the rule for the hour, the whole verse card and all four of the Church's cards. The wait before it appears looks like the page now as well. It had been borrowing the phone's loading shape, which on a computer was one large pulsing grey block.

sections.heading: The Today page can be read by more people
sections.body: Every small label on it was drawn faint. The labelling the whole page is built from sat at just under four to one against the background, and the arrow at the end of each prayer row at a little over two to one, where the readable standard is four and a half to one. They have been lifted out of that range, and the labels on the Church's cards sit near six to one. The page also had one heading and then eight blocks with no heading at all, which a screen reader met as a wall, and one line that was styled to look like a heading without being one. Every section carries a real heading now, in order, with no level skipped. And each prayer row shows a clear ring when you reach it by keyboard and lights as you pass over it with a mouse, which the rows did not do before. Those rows are listed in six places in the app, so that part reaches well beyond this page.

sections.heading: The date reads in your language
sections.body: The heading on the Today page was assembled from a list of English weekday and month names, so it read Sunday, August 2, 2026 in all twenty-one languages Purify offers. It reads in yours now. Nine more strings on the same page were English in every language for the same reason: the whole of the section that remembers where you left off, the anniversaries in your diptych, and the two notes the verse card shows when you save a verse.

sections.heading: Accounts made with Google were never shown the Terms
sections.body: Creating an account through Google presented no Terms notice of any kind, while the two email forms both did. Five hundred and seventy-two accounts were made that way and were never shown them. Signing in and signing up with Google now carry the notice, and it sits above the buttons rather than below them, so it is passed on the way to the account and not after it.

sections.heading: The Android app had never reported a session
sections.body: Not a screen view, not a session, nothing, for as long as it has been installed on anything. The cause was narrow. The app runs from its own address on the device and posts to purifyapp.net, and the endpoint receiving those posts refused anything that did not come from the website itself, so every pageview from an installed app was turned away. The endpoint now recognises the app's own shells by name, and nothing else. Reporting works from this build onward, which means the record starts when the next Android build is installed rather than filling in anything already on a phone.

sections.heading: Prayer reminders had nothing to send them
sections.body: Two scheduled jobs existed in the code, one to deliver prayer reminders and one to record the day's donations, and nothing anywhere called either of them. A schedule exists now and is kept in the repository so it can be read and changed like everything else, but it will not run until one secret is set in two places, and the donations record waits on that same secret. Delivery waits on more than that: no phone has ever been able to register for a notification, because the step that asks your permission is itself waiting on its keys, so there is nothing yet to send to. What arrives here is the mechanism, and an honest count. The sending panel used to write a line saying a broadcast had gone out when it had resolved nobody to send it to, which happened three times in July. It now refuses the send and says which part failed.

sections.heading: The app will tell you when there is a new version
sections.body: Purify cannot make your phone update itself. Whether an app updates on its own is a setting in the Play Store, on your device, and no app is allowed to reach in and change it. What Purify can stop doing is leaving you to find out on your own. When you open it and the version you have is behind the one on the store, it now says so, with a button that takes you to the listing and a Later that costs nothing. It asks once each time you open the app, not once per screen. It will not make the download smaller, and that is the part worth being honest about: Purify is a large app because the whole library travels with it and works with no signal, and a large update is exactly the kind the Play Store holds back until you are on wi-fi. Making that download much smaller is the next piece of work.

sections.heading: A run of Android repairs
sections.body: The app was registering the website's background worker, which could serve it a stale copy of the site instead of its own. That worker is now cleared away on launch, along with the copies it had kept, so a tester stuck on an old bundle comes right the next time the app opens, and reinstalling gives a clean slate rather than restoring what was there before. The bar at the top of the screen had been slipping under the status bar, because the spacing around the notch and the home bar was being read as nothing at all. It is handled by one thing now instead of two disagreeing. The gap above the keyboard is no longer a grey box. As with everything on this list that lives in the app rather than on the site, none of it reaches a phone until the next build is installed.

sections.heading: Form fields no longer zoom the page
sections.body: Tapping a text field on a phone zoomed the whole page in, because the text inside the field was under sixteen pixels and the browser magnifies to compensate. Every form control is pinned to sixteen now.

sections.heading: Housekeeping
sections.body: A developer panel for the accounts on the allow list, reached from a row only those accounts see on the mobile account screen, which can switch on a test subscription without touching a real one. New checks run over the saints' library with every change: they refuse a registered work with no file behind it, a file that disagrees with the registry, a writing nothing cites, and a date in the month pointing at nobody, and they flag an em dash anywhere a reader can see one, with the ten that already exist listed by name so the debt stays visible and nothing new joins it. The blurb on the Apostles now names the Seventy He sent ahead of Him two by two. The cache version steps to purify-beta-3.0.0, so a returning reader is served this build rather than the last one.

title: The app moves like one thing
intro: Almost all of this one is about how Purify answers your thumb rather than what is in it. Moving between the seven tabs was a hard cut: one screen vanished, the next appeared already finished, and on a slower phone there was a blank moment in between with nothing to say that your tap had registered. Screens now leave and arrive. Titles and cards settle rather than snap. And the Fathers' commentary, which a reader in the Android beta reported twice, is finally clear of the tab bar.

sections.heading: The tab bar no longer covers the commentary
sections.body: A reader in the Android beta reported twice that the last lines of a Father were unreachable, and then that a second commentary on the same verse could not be opened at all. Both were the same fault: the bar at the foot of the app was drawn on top of the sheet, covering the bottom of it. Text sat behind the bar, and any commentary heading that scrolled into that band took the tap itself instead of passing it on. A fix in July added space at the bottom of the sheet, which moved the text but left the bar taking the taps, because space underneath cannot stop something drawn on top. The bar now steps aside for as long as the sheet is open, which is what it should have done from the start: while you are reading a commentary, nothing else belongs over it.

sections.heading: The mark that opens a commentary is big enough to hit
sections.body: On a phone, a verse with commentary carries a small red verse number and a dot. Tapping it opens the sheet. That mark measured five pixels tall, so a tap landed beside it more often than on it, and there was nothing to tell you that you had missed rather than that nothing was there. The area that answers your thumb is now about twenty five pixels square, which is the size a touch target is meant to be. The mark itself is unchanged: it is the same size, the same colour, in the same place, and the lines of the verse have not moved by a pixel. Only the part that listens for your thumb is larger, and it was never visible in the first place.

sections.heading: Moving between tabs is one motion instead of a cut
sections.body: Tapping a tab now begins fading the screen you are leaving in the same instant as the tap, before the app has even started building the one you asked for, and the new screen fades in as it arrives. Leaving takes about a seventh of a second and arriving about a quarter, because a screen on its way out should stop competing for your attention quickly while a screen on its way in deserves long enough to register. The bar itself never fades, so the tab you pressed lights up immediately and the app answers you before the page does. Tapping the tab you are already on does nothing, as before, rather than flickering the screen for a journey with no destination.

sections.heading: Screens settle into place
sections.body: A screen's title, and then the cards under it, now rise a few pixels as they fade in, each one a fraction behind the one above. The distances are small on purpose, six pixels for a title and eight for a card: past about ten it stops reading as a page settling and starts reading as a list performing for you. The interval between them is thirty eight thousandths of a second, which is felt without being counted. The reading screens are deliberately left out of this, because their chapter pill, verse toolbar, progress bar and commentary sheet are pinned to the glass, and anything that moves the page underneath them drags them out of position. That is the same fault as the tab bar over the commentary, and it is now written down in the stylesheet and guarded by a test so it cannot be reintroduced by accident.

sections.heading: Everything you press answers the same way
sections.body: How far a control dips when you hold it is now two numbers for the whole app, one for small things like pills and icon buttons and one for large tappable cards and rows, rather than being retyped at every place that wanted the effect. Seven places on the mobile screens had rolled their own slightly different version; they use the shared ones now. The dip is the same as it always was on the places that already had it. What changed is that it is now consistent, and can be retuned in one line.

sections.heading: Waiting looks like the screen you are waiting for
sections.body: Discover, Prayers, Account and the campaigns list showed a line of grey text while they loaded, or nothing at all. Each now shows the shape of the screen that is coming: a plate where the picture will be, short bars where the headings will be. This is not decoration. It means the layout does not jump when the content lands, and it tells you the app is working rather than stuck.

sections.heading: If you have asked your phone for less motion, there is none
sections.body: Every animation added here, and the ones that were already there, are switched off when your device is set to reduce motion. Not shortened, switched off: screens cut rather than fade, nothing rises, nothing dips. The system setting is the whole instruction and Purify does not second-guess it.

sections.heading: Also
sections.body: The two thin gold progress bars, the one at the top of a chapter and the one on a saint's work, are now the same piece of the app rather than two copies of the same eight lines. A confirmation tick can now draw itself in. Cache version steps to purify-beta-2.9.0.

title: Daniel is whole again, and the app stops saying everything twice
intro: Two things lead this one. Three passages that were missing from Daniel are restored, which is what the last update said would happen. And the app has stopped repeating itself: the same page was offered to you under three different names, screens announced themselves twice before you had read a word, and the prayer index printed thirty-four rows for twenty-seven prayers. Underneath all of it sat one real fault worth naming on its own: readers who keep the Old Calendar were being shown the wrong saint and the wrong fast on the daily prayer page. There is also a Settings screen now, the reading palettes colour the whole app rather than two screens, and two more councils have been added.

sections.heading: Susanna, Bel and the Dragon, and the middle of Daniel 3
sections.body: Someone asked whether Bel and the Dragon was missing from Daniel. It was, and so was more than that. Susanna was absent, and chapter 3 was short its middle, where the Prayer of Azariah and the Song of the Three Holy Children belong. The last update said these were coming; here they are. Daniel now has fourteen chapters: Susanna is chapter 13 with sixty-four verses, Bel is chapter 14 with forty-two, and chapter 3 now runs to verse 97, with the three young men falling bound into the furnace at verse 23, the Song from 24 to 90, and Nabuchodonosor hearing them sing at 91. Brenton's numbering has no verses 67 to 70, so the chapter holds ninety-three verses across a range that ends at 97. Every verse is from the same public domain Brenton Septuagint the rest of the Old Testament is set in. Two things worth knowing. Verses 1 to 23 of chapter 3 are where they always were, but sixty-three verses were restored in the middle, so anything you had highlighted or bookmarked in that chapter after verse 23 now sits at a different number, and what used to be 3:31 to 3:33 has moved into chapter 4. And the Greek column is blank alongside the Song itself: the Greek edition we carry orders that canticle differently from Brenton, and showing you a Greek verse that is not the one you are reading would be worse than showing you none.

sections.heading: The Old Calendar was ignored on the daily prayer page
sections.body: If you keep the Old (Julian) Calendar, the daily prayer page was showing you the New Calendar's commemoration and the New Calendar's fasting rule, while the Today screen one tap away showed the right ones. Two screens, two different saints, the same second. The page now keeps the calendar you keep. The appointed readings and the count to Pascha deliberately do not shift with it, because both reckonings work out Pascha the same way.

sections.heading: Recently saved items led nowhere
sections.body: The Last saved cards on the account dashboard were built from the wrong description of a bookmark, so every one of them linked to a chapter that does not exist. They open what you saved.

sections.heading: One name for one place
sections.body: The daily prayer page was reachable from inside the app as a tile called Today in Prayers, a tile called Daily readings in Discover, and a chip called Prayer on your account screen, all leading to the same screen, which is itself the page the website opens for Today. Tapping the one in Prayers also moved the lit tab to Today, so you were standing in one section with a different one highlighted. The tiles are gone and the highlight tells the truth. The reading room listed the saints twice under two names, as Patristic works and The saints' writings, both going to the same place with nothing to tell them apart. It lists them once.

sections.heading: Each prayer is listed once
sections.body: The Prayers index showed the popular rules and then showed every category in full, without leaving out what it had just shown, so seven prayers appeared twice on the same screen and two more repeated the tiles above them. Thirty-four rows for twenty-seven prayers. Every prayer is still there and every prayer is listed once. The suggestions for the hour still sit at the top, because a prayer that fits right now is worth offering even when it also appears further down.

sections.heading: Screens say their name once
sections.body: Discover said Discover in the bar, again over the picture, and a third time on the tab below it, before you had read a word. Reading did the same. The picture keeps its place and its credit and stops repeating the title. Three title bars were also being drawn on Discover, Reading and Prayers that no screen size could ever show, which is why those screens had no back bar.

sections.heading: The account screen no longer repeats itself
sections.body: Opening Account and security from the You tab landed you on a screen that repeated eight of the nine rows you had just left, under a second copy of your name and a second copy of the same four counters. On a phone that screen is now the security, sessions and data screen it was meant to be, and the two rows that only lived there, Export your library and My prayers, have moved onto the You tab so nothing was lost. On a computer, where that screen is the whole dashboard, it is unchanged.

sections.heading: The tab bar fits other languages
sections.body: In Greek, Russian, Romanian and French the bar ran off the side of the screen and the last tab was partly or wholly unreachable. The seven tabs now divide the width evenly in every language.

sections.heading: A tablet knows what day it is
sections.body: Beta 2.7 unfroze the date everywhere a phone could see it and missed the wider layout, which a tablet shows. On a tablet, Discover's featured topic and council, and the day card on Prayers, were still stuck on the day the app was built. They read the date from the device now, like everything else. The guard that is supposed to catch this class of fault was only watching part of the app, which is why it did not catch it. It watches all of it now.

sections.heading: The palette you pick is now the app's palette
sections.body: Candlelight, Monastery and Parchment only ever coloured the two reading screens, and the moment you left one you were back on the standard night palette. They colour the whole app now, and the choice is remembered, so opening Purify in the morning finds it the way you left it rather than flashing the old colours first. The palettes themselves are unchanged.

sections.heading: There is a Settings screen
sections.body: There was not one before. The reading font and size, the interlinear default and the calendar reckoning were behind a sign-in, on a tab called Data, which is also where the row marked Notifications led. None of those ever needed an account, and they do not need one now: Settings opens whether you are signed in or not, and the palette sits at the top of it. The things that genuinely need an account, reminders and exporting your library, are linked from there rather than moved, so there is still one of each.

sections.heading: Two more councils, and a line saying how each was received
sections.body: The Synod of Jerusalem of 1672, which answered the Calvinist confession printed under Cyril Lucaris' name and is the fullest statement the Church made in the modern period, and the Second Council of Orange of 529, which the Orthodox Church does not receive and which is here because it is cited so often in Western writing on grace that a reader is likely to meet it and deserves to be told plainly where it stands. Every council page that needs one now carries a line about how the Church received it, placed above what the council defined rather than below. The Councils of Carthage of 256 have gained that line too: St. Cyprian is honoured as a hieromartyr, and his rule that everyone coming from heresy must be baptised is not the rule the Church settled on.

sections.heading: A review only says Verified buyer when it is one
sections.body: Reviews of a store carried a Verified buyer badge whether or not there was a delivered order behind them. Product reviews had already been corrected for this; store reviews had not. The badge now appears only where a real purchase backs it. The reviews themselves are unchanged; only the claim about them is.

sections.heading: The anthem can be paused from anywhere
sections.body: You could start the Prayer Rope Anthem, walk to another screen, and have no way to stop it short of going back and finding the page again. A small bar now sits at the foot of the app whenever something is playing, with the track, the time, and a play and pause you can reach from any screen. It stays out of the way on the anthem page itself, where the full player is already in front of you. And the prayer rope's bead no longer strikes over the top of the chant: the music steps back while the tone sounds and comes up again as it fades.

sections.heading: When someone answers you, you will know
sections.body: Until now a reply reached nobody. If someone answered your post you found out by opening the tab again and scrolling down to look. Replies now come back to you: a mark on the Community tab when something is waiting, and a short list at the top of Conversations of who answered and what they said. Nothing is sent to your email and nothing is pushed to your phone.

sections.heading: Also
sections.body: The Today screen had four buttons to Prayers, Bible, Saints and Calendar sitting just above the bar that already carries those, and it called the Bible Scripture while the tab beside it said Bible. They are gone and the day's commemoration has moved up the screen. Cache version steps to purify-beta-2.8.0.

title: The app knows what day it is
intro: One real bug, and it was the big one. The app was showing the day it was built rather than the day it is. If your Today screen has been stuck on a date that never moved, this is the release that fixes it. You will need this update installed for the fix to reach you.

sections.heading: The day was frozen at the moment the app was built
sections.body: Today, Prayers, Discover and the daily prayer page all read the date once, when the app was assembled, and then kept it. That is why the day, the saint of the day, the fast, the appointed readings and the count to Pascha could sit still for weeks at a time. Every one of those surfaces now reads the date from your own phone, and rolls over at midnight while the app is open or the next time you come back to it.

sections.heading: And it is your date now, not the world's
sections.body: Underneath the freeze was a second, quieter fault: the app worked in UTC. From about seven in the evening across the United States that is already tomorrow, so you were shown tomorrow's commemoration and tomorrow's fasting rule while it was still today where you were standing. The morning, midday and evening lines on the Prayers tab had the same trouble, and could greet you with "stand before God before the day takes you" at nine at night.

sections.heading: Changing a reading mode no longer throws you back to Today
sections.body: Tapping a palette you do not have yet was meant to open the Pro page. It opened it in a way the app could not resolve, and the app answered by putting you back on the home screen. Two other buttons had exactly the same fault and were repaired at the same time.

sections.heading: The historical timeline is quick on a phone again
sections.body: Scrolling the timeline measured every card on the list on every single frame and wrote your position to storage twice a frame, which on a mid range phone is most of a tap's worth of work happening continuously. Opening an event then animated its height, which re-laid out every card beneath it for the length of the animation. Both are gone, and the icon of the First Council of Nicaea is now a two hundred kilobyte file rather than a two megabyte one.

sections.heading: St Diodore of Tarsus has been removed from the saints
sections.body: He was condemned after his death as a forerunner of Nestorianism and is not commemorated by the Church. He should not have been in the registry, on the calendar for October 22, or listed among the fathers of the Second Ecumenical Council, and he is in none of them now.

sections.heading: Bel and the Dragon is coming to Daniel
sections.body: Someone asked whether Bel and the Dragon was missing from Daniel. It is, and so is more than that: Susanna is absent too, and chapter 3 is short its middle, where the Prayer of Azariah and the Song of the Three Holy Children belong. They will be restored as Daniel 13 and 14, and chapter 3 will be made whole, from the same public domain Brenton Septuagint the rest of the Old Testament is set in. The text is prepared and lands in the next update.

title: Six new studies, the saints in Discover, and a cross where the goalpost was
intro: A large content release and a handful of fixes you asked for by name. The theology library grew by six long-form studies and opened a new shelf on the worship of the Church. Discover finally has the saints on it. And the Prayers tab is no longer wearing a goalpost.

sections.heading: The worship of the Church, a new shelf
sections.body: Two studies open a new section in the theology library. The Divine Liturgy of St John Chrysostom is walked in the order it is actually served, from the cutting of the Lamb at the table of preparation, through the antiphons and the reading of the Word, the dismissal of the catechumens, the Great Entrance and the calling down of the Spirit, to communion. Beside it, the vestments: every garment with its name, its root in Exodus, and the prayer the priest says while putting it on.

sections.heading: Four studies from the dogma side
sections.body: Why the Orthodox Church does not receive the Council of Florence, and what makes a synod a Council in the first place. What St Theodore the Studite was actually asking of Rome when he wrote to it from exile, read alongside the letters he sent to Alexandria, Antioch and Jerusalem at the same time. Whether St Justin Martyr can fairly be called a subordinationist, and the difference between order and inequality in God. And penal substitution: how the Cross both heals and pays, and what the Fathers refuse.

sections.heading: Every quotation checked against its source
sections.body: The part you cannot see. All 75 quotations in the six new studies were matched word by word against the public domain edition each one cites, and two were removed because they could not be confirmed. One of them was a well known text that turned out to be a modern wording carrying a very old citation. A checker now lives in the repository so this happens every time rather than once.

sections.heading: The saints, in Discover
sections.body: Discover lists the saints now, first in the library on a phone and as a third door on a wide screen. The strings for it had been written months ago and were never connected to anything.

sections.heading: Orthodox imagery across the app
sections.body: Five surfaces that were built out of line drawings on grey now open on a real image, each one public domain and recorded: the Codex Sinaiticus on Scripture, the Deesis on Prayers, the Menologion of Basil II on Discover, the Evangelist Luke from the Ostromir Gospels on Reading, and the Ladder of Divine Ascent on your own page.

sections.heading: A cross where the goalpost was
sections.body: The Prayers tab carried a mark meant to be the ancient prayer posture, arms raised. Drawn without a head or hands and shrunk to the size of a tab, it was two uprights and a crossbar. It is the Orthodox three bar cross now.

sections.heading: The screen no longer stretches
sections.body: Scrolling past the end of a page pulled the whole screen away from the edge and let it snap back, which is a browser habit and not something an app should do. The rule meant to stop it had been written on the wrong element and had never once applied.

sections.heading: Multi reference search works in the app
sections.body: Searching two or more references at once, like 1 Tim 2:5, Prov 8:7, used to drop you back on Today with your query lost whenever you were in the Android app. The page it sends you to had been left out of the app bundle. It ships now, and the service it reads verse text from will answer the app, which it previously refused to do.

sections.heading: The end of a commentary is readable again
sections.body: The patristic commentary panel sits against the bottom of the screen, and the last lines of a Father were ending up underneath the tab bar and the phone's gesture area. It now keeps clear space beneath it. The panel can also be pulled down to close, which the handle at its top had been promising for some time.

sections.heading: A weekly note instead of a stale one
sections.body: The message at the top of this page used to be rewritten only when a large release shipped, so it sat introducing Beta 1.7 while the app had moved on eight releases. It is a weekly note now, and if a week is missed it says nothing rather than something out of date.

title: A lighter app and a clearer bar
intro: Two things you should notice. The bar along the bottom has been redrawn, and Purify now takes up a good deal less room on your phone. About a quarter of what the app was carrying turned out to be the same pages stored over and over, and that is gone.

sections.heading: The bottom bar, redrawn
sections.body: New marks for Scripture, Discover, Prayers, Shop and your account, each drawn to sit at the same weight as the ones beside it. The old set had icons that rendered nearly twice the size of their neighbours and several that ran past their own edges. The circle that used to slide around behind the selected tab is gone; the tab itself now brightens and lifts instead.

sections.heading: Less to carry
sections.body: Roughly a quarter of the app was the same content written out several times over by the build. Removing the duplicates takes nothing away from what you can read: every prayer, life and chapter is still there and still works with no signal.

sections.heading: Quieter while you scroll
sections.body: The saints list and the Bible chapter strip used to quietly load pages you had not opened while you scrolled past them. On a phone that competed with the scrolling itself. They now wait until you actually choose something.

sections.heading: A small answer to every tap
sections.body: Choosing a tab gives a short tick you can feel, and the icon settles in rather than snapping. If you have asked your phone to reduce motion, it stays still.

title: A calmer hand on the phone
intro: Nothing new to learn in this one. Purify simply moves better. Screens now settle the way you read them, from the top down, instead of arriving all at once, and the cards and rows you tap finally answer to your finger. On Android the app scrolls more smoothly, and if you have asked your phone to reduce motion, more of Purify now listens.

sections.heading: Screens arrive in order
sections.body: The greeting, then the day's word, then the prayer rule, then the doors below, each settling a moment after the one above it. A page now reads as it appears rather than landing in one piece.

sections.heading: Everything you tap answers
sections.body: The saint of the day, the fast, the appointed readings, and the count to Pascha used to sit still under your finger on a phone. They now press in and spring back like the rest of the app.

sections.heading: Loading looks like the thing it is loading
sections.body: Waiting states across Scripture, the saints, the calendar, the councils, and history were each drawn a little differently. They now share one shape, and content no longer jumps when it arrives.

sections.heading: A clearer Today, a shorter door to the saints
sections.body: The Today screen's Explore doors were four almost-identical shades of grey pretending to be different; they are one clean surface now, told apart by their icons. And the Saints page opens onto saints, where its heading used to fill a phone screen on its own.

sections.heading: Smoother, and quieter when you ask
sections.body: Several blur effects were removed from the places you scroll past in the Android app; they cost frames on a phone and gave nothing back. Reduce Motion is honored in more places, including sheets and dialogs, and a change to the setting now takes effect at once instead of on the next launch.

title: Purify learns your language
intro: This release opens Purify to the whole household of the faith: the app now speaks twenty-one languages. Pick yours in Settings or in the footer, and the menus, the Today screen, the calendar with every fasting rule, and the app's chrome follow you, on the website and inside the Android app, even offline. The prayers, lives, and writings themselves are being translated next; until each one lands, it is shown in English with an honest note. The core of Purify stays free, today and always.

sections.heading: Twenty-one languages
sections.body: English, Spanish, Romanian, Greek, Russian, French, German, Serbian, Ukrainian, Italian, Portuguese, Bulgarian, Arabic, Filipino, Turkish, Georgian, Hungarian, Indonesian, Nepali, Polish, and Urdu. Every language is available to everyone from day one, and the site greets first-time visitors in their browser's own language. Our language editors keep refining the translations in place; anything not yet translated falls back to English rather than breaking.

sections.heading: The app finally switches
sections.body: Language switching now works inside the Android app, not just on the website. Your choice is remembered on the device, follows your account when you sign in, and on first run the app greets you in your phone's own language when we carry it.

sections.heading: Every script renders true
sections.body: New typefaces for Cyrillic, Greek, Arabic script, Georgian, and Devanagari, loaded only when a page actually needs them, so no language reads as empty boxes.

sections.heading: A language home in Settings
sections.body: A Language row now leads your account settings, with the same grouped picker as the footer: available languages, previews under review, and the ones still to come.

title: The shop finds its voice, and its word of honor
intro: This release lets the EIKON shop speak and be spoken to. You can now reach the Purify team from inside the shop, hear back in a living conversation, and mark a message with a small heart. And the word of others carries real weight: reviews now come only from those who received what they bought, so a rating is a testimony, not a guess. The core of Purify stays free, today and always.

sections.heading: A word of honor on every review
sections.body: A review now stands on what actually arrived. You may leave one for a product only after your order is marked delivered, so a rating is the testimony of someone who held the thing in their hands. Every review carries a verified-buyer mark naming what was bought. And you can now review a whole shop, not only its products, so a maker's care over many orders is seen as one.

sections.heading: The shop can speak, and be spoken to
sections.body: A new door, Contact EIKON support, sits in the shop and in your messages: it opens a real conversation with the Purify team about an order or a question, and picks the thread back up where you left it. Inside a conversation you now see the honest state of your last message, delivered when it has arrived and read when it has been seen, so you are never left wondering.

sections.heading: A small heart, where it belongs
sections.body: Messages in the shop can now be marked with a heart: a double-tap on a phone, or a quiet heart button, to say a thing landed without needing more words. It is a small warmth in a place that was only ever plain text before.

sections.heading: A cleaner desk on our side
sections.body: The team's support desk and the admin were given a calmer, clearer hand so your questions are answered with less friction and less delay. Cache version steps to purify-beta-2.2.

title: The plan finds its shape, and reading finds its light
intro: This release gives the three plans their true shape and brings the first of Pro's premium layer to life. Standard remains the complete Orthodox foundation, free forever. Purify Plus is now purely the premium reading and study experience. And Purify Pro becomes the complete premium experience: new reading modes that change the very light of the page, the EIKON Box on its way, and the shop's member benefits gathered in one place. The core of Purify stays free, today and always.

sections.heading: Three plans, cleanly cut
sections.body: Standard carries the whole foundation: the Scriptures, the saints and the Fathers, theology and the Councils, Orthodox History, the prayers, the calendar with its fasts, and Prayer Campaigns. No ads, no tracking, no surprise locks. Purify Plus is the premium reading and study experience: your library, notes, highlights, and collections on every device you sign in on. Purify Pro is everything in Plus and the complete premium experience. Free EIKON shipping now belongs to Pro's member benefits, alongside member discount codes and early access.

sections.heading: Premium Reading Modes
sections.body: Reading has found its light. Four modes now live in the reader settings: Focus, which clears everything but the text; Candlelight, warm amber for the late hours; Monastery, cool stone and quiet indigo; and Parchment, aged paper with dark ink. They re-light the Scriptures and the writings of the Fathers alike, and your choice is remembered on your device. Reading modes are part of Purify Pro; while the beta is open they are free for everyone to try.

sections.heading: Purify Pro, in the app
sections.body: The subscription screen in the Android app now carries both tiers: a quiet switch under the hero moves between Plus and Pro, each with its own live prices from Google Play and its own list of what is included. Anyone who holds Plus and steps up to Pro is told honestly how to end the old plan so no one pays twice.

sections.heading: The EIKON Box, on its way
sections.body: Pro's box is coming: a curated monthly box of Orthodox devotional goods, an icon, a prayer rope, incense, a booklet, or seasonal gifts, with contents that vary month to month. Studio Audio, professionally narrated Scripture, saints, and history, is also on the road ahead. Both are named on the plan today and will light up as they arrive; nothing is charged for what has not yet shipped.

title: A cleaner walk through the whole app
intro: A polish release. Purify Premium now has a home of its own, Discover reads more calmly, and the Fasting, Prayer Campaigns, and Trapeza screens move with a lighter hand on the phone. A fault that could leave a signed-in reader stuck on 'opening the campaign' is fixed, and the EIKON shop shows its icons in full again and asks you, after an order, to share an honest word. The core of Purify stays free, today and always.

sections.heading: Purify Premium, in one place
sections.body: A new Premium page lays out the three plans side by side, Standard, Plus, and Pro, with everything each one carries and the opening half-off-first-year offer. A quiet marker in the header leads you there whenever you want to look. Nothing about the free core changes.

sections.heading: A calmer Discover
sections.body: Discover was carrying duplicate doorways and a wall of small buttons. It now reads in a few clear rooms, and the doctrinal library, Theology, Apologetics, Topics, and the heresies the Church answered, gathers under one hub instead of four scattered tiles.

sections.heading: Prayer Campaigns open every time
sections.body: A signed-in reader could land on a campaign that stayed stuck on 'opening the campaign' when their session was slow to confirm. The campaign now appears as soon as it loads, and a failure offers a way back instead of a spinner that never ends. Starting a campaign is a gentler, carded flow too.

sections.heading: Lighter on the phone
sections.body: The Fasting, Prayer Campaigns, and Trapeza screens share one quiet, minimal design now, with a soft entrance as each section settles in and a small give under your thumb. Cleaner, calmer, and quicker to read.

sections.heading: The EIKON shop, set right
sections.body: Featured icons were hiding all but one behind a stricter image check; the shelf is full again, and every card lines up to the same baseline. After an order is placed, the shop now invites you to leave an honest, verified review to help the next person praying.

title: The fast kept, the table shared, and prayers held in common
intro: Welcome, and glory to Jesus Christ. This is the fullest release yet. You can keep the fast day by day now, share a prayer in common, and set the table with recipes for the season. Your gathered library can be carried anywhere and kept as your own copy. The one true cross stands over the whole app, the top of every screen sits right, sign-in and your account hold steady, and the EIKON shop has been rebuilt around search and clean cards. The core of Purify, the Scriptures, the prayers, the saints, the calendar, and the new fasting tracker, is free, today and always.

sections.heading: Keep the fast, day by day
sections.body: A new fasting tracker meets you where the calendar already is. It tells you plainly what today's fast asks, and lets you mark the day: kept, in part, or broke. A gentle streak counts the days you have kept, forgiving today until it is out and never scolding. Kept, not tracked, with room for the sick, the travelling, expecting mothers, and catechumens, and always under your priest's blessing. It works free and offline, kept on your device.

sections.heading: Pray together
sections.body: Prayer Campaigns are a place to ask the Church to pray with you: for healing, for comfort and strength, for the persecuted, in thanksgiving, or for the departed, memory eternal. Start one in a few words, join the ones that move you, and mark that you have prayed. First names only, and only what you have a blessing to share. It is, and stays, free.

sections.heading: The Trapeza, the shared table
sections.body: The Trapeza is a board of fasting-friendly recipes, sorted by the fast, the season, and the tradition. A few plain dishes from the Purify kitchen to begin, and you can send your own for the board.

sections.heading: Carry your library, and keep a copy
sections.body: You can now export your notes, highlights, bookmarks, and collections and keep them as your own copy, yours to hold whatever comes.

sections.heading: One cross, everywhere
sections.body: The three-bar Orthodox cross now stands over the whole app: the mark beside the name, the browser tab, and the icon on your home screen. One cross, the true one, in every place Purify appears.

sections.heading: Purify's plan, made plain
sections.body: The plan now reads in three clear parts. Standard is free and always will be: the Scriptures, the prayers, the saints, the calendar, the fasting tracker, and the community. Purify Plus carries your library across every device. And a new Purify Pro adds a members' layer, a devotional icon mailed each month and codes for the EIKON shop. Everything you use today stays free.

sections.heading: The top bar sits right
sections.body: The status-bar inset was being applied twice, which left a dead band under the top bar across the app. It is applied once now, and the gap is gone.

sections.heading: Sign-in and your account hold steady
sections.body: Several deep faults in how the app confirmed your sign-in have been closed. The account gate now trusts your device's own session instead of a network check that could hang, and the Profile and Security screens read the same way, so the account pages open when they should.

sections.heading: The reader obeys the back button
sections.body: On Android, the back button now closes the reader's settings sheet instead of leaving the page, and the handler no longer churns or leaks.

sections.heading: The EIKON shop, rebuilt
sections.body: The marketplace now has search, filters, and premium cards, and a category page that used to break now holds. New icons join the shelves, and the first prayer ropes: knotted wool komboskini for the Jesus Prayer.

sections.heading: Small comforts
sections.body: The app no longer bounces past the top and bottom of a page, the rubber-band pull that never belonged in a prayer book. The reminder time pickers now render in the dark with a clear focus ring. The cache version steps to purify-beta-2.0.

closing: Many of these came from your reports. If anything still misbehaves, write to lifeistheosis@gmail.com. I read every one, and I pray for the people who send them.

title: Sign-in that cannot jam, and a Plus screen worthy of the name
intro: Welcome, and glory to Jesus Christ. Two pieces of work in this patch. First, the deepest sign-in fault we have found yet: a single stuck tab could quietly jam the machinery every other tab uses to confirm your sign-in, and the app could only offer a retry that never succeeded. That machinery now frees itself. Second, the Purify Plus screen has been made worthy of what it sells: the true Purify cross, honest spacing, and the full list of what Plus actually includes. The core of Purify stays free, today and always.

sections.heading: Sign-in frees itself now
sections.body: Your browser coordinates sign-in checks across tabs through a shared lock. If one tab froze while holding it, every other tab waited forever, and the account page could only say it could not confirm your sign-in. The app now waits five seconds, then proceeds without the lock. The worst case of proceeding is a harmless duplicate token refresh; the worst case of waiting was an account page that never opened. We reproduced the jam deliberately and the page now resolves in seconds, and that exact scenario runs as an automated test on every build.

sections.heading: The Plus screen, made worthy
sections.body: The subscription screen now wears the true Purify cross, the same minimalist three-bar mark as the wordmark, instead of a heavier redraw. The dead band above the hero is gone; the screen breathes the way it was designed to. And the included list now tells the whole truth: cross-device sync, notes and highlights and bookmarks, custom collections and the Florilegium, free EIKON shipping on every order while Plus is active, and Immersive History, the cinematic dress on the story of the Church. Every line names something that works today.

closing: Both fixes came from your reports, one from a screenshot sent the same hour. If anything else misbehaves, write to lifeistheosis@gmail.com. I read every email, and I pray for the people who send them.

title: Purify Plus opens again, and highlights learn to look like ink
intro: Welcome, and glory to Jesus Christ. This patch mends the most serious kind of bug we can ship: tapping Purify Plus closed the app outright. The fault was two billing components speaking different versions of the same language deep in the Android layer, and it is fixed at the root. While we were in the reader we also freed anyone the app had trapped in focus mode, and gave highlights the look they always deserved: ink on the words, not a bar in the margin. The core of Purify stays free, today and always.

sections.heading: Purify Plus opens again
sections.body: Tapping Purify Plus crashed the app the moment the subscription screen tried to wake the billing machinery. Two of its components had drifted onto incompatible versions, and the collision brought the whole app down. They now move in lockstep, and the paywall opens, prices load from Google Play, and Restore works as intended. If Plus ever cannot load, you will see a calm explanation instead of a crash.

sections.heading: A guaranteed way out of focus mode
sections.body: Focus reading hides the app around the text. A recent restructuring accidentally left the top bar standing invisible over the Exit button, swallowing every tap, and on a phone there is no Escape key to fall back on. The exit now floats above everything by construction, the app chrome truly steps aside, and a new automated test presses the real button on every build so this cannot quietly return.

sections.heading: Highlights look like ink now
sections.body: A highlighted verse used to wear a plain colored bar down its left margin. It now carries a quiet wash of its color across the words themselves, line by line, the way a real highlighter moves. Word-level highlights stay brighter inside it, and the writings of the saints receive the same treatment in gold.

closing: The Plus crash was reported by a reader and reproduced within the hour. If anything else misbehaves, write to lifeistheosis@gmail.com. I read every email, and I pray for the people who send them.

title: One hand for every symbol, and two checkout bugs caught live
intro: Welcome, and glory to Jesus Christ. Two kinds of work in this patch. First, we walked the live shop the way a customer would and caught two real bugs at the door: a product page that could sit loading forever, and a checkout that returned buyers to a dead page after paying or backing out. Both are fixed and the whole cancel path is now verified against live Stripe. Second, every symbol in the app's buttons and controls now comes from one hand: our own icon family, drawn on one grid with one stroke, replacing the mismatched keyboard characters and third-party glyphs that had crept in. The core of Purify stays free, today and always.

sections.heading: Checkout, walked and mended
sections.body: Backing out of a live payment used to strand you on a broken page, and the same flaw would have caught paying customers after checkout. Return addresses now always point home. We also proved the abandon path end to end against live Stripe: leave the payment page and the attempt cancels itself, with nothing charged and nothing lingering in your orders.

sections.heading: Pages that never say almost
sections.body: A product page could hang on its loading bones if the app was waiting on a stale sign-in check held by another tab. Pages now refuse to wait on niceties: the shipping perk check gives itself a short deadline and steps aside, and the page simply loads.

sections.heading: The webhook grew armor
sections.body: The machinery that marks orders paid now verifies the charged amount against the order before believing anything, and if a payment lands on an order that was cancelled a heartbeat earlier, the payment wins and the order is restored. Eleven new tests hold these rules in place.

sections.heading: One family of symbols
sections.body: The bookmark star, the note pen, the copy link, the highlight spark, the cart plus and minus, the close cross, the menu lines, the rating stars, the save heart: all now drawn in Purify's own hand, on one grid, with one stroke, crisp in every button on every screen. The link symbol no longer turns into a colored emoji on Android, and the same action now wears the same symbol everywhere it appears.

sections.heading: A clearer footing on the bottom bar
sections.body: The selected tab now speaks three ways: its color, its sliding backdrop, and a slightly firmer line in the icon itself, so the active tab reads clearly without leaning on color alone.

closing: Found by walking the aisles ourselves, mended the same afternoon. If anything else is loose, write to lifeistheosis@gmail.com. I read every email, and I pray for the people who send them.

title: The shop, refined: a cart, honest orders, and a smoother checkout
intro: Welcome, and glory to Jesus Christ. The shop opened its doors inside the app this morning, and the first walkers-through found the loose boards by evening. This patch mends every one of them and adds the piece most shops are born with: a cart. Icons pages no longer error on desktop, walking away from checkout no longer leaves a ghost in your orders, and paying for an icon now ends with a moment worthy of the purchase. The core of Purify stays free, today and always.

sections.heading: A cart, at last
sections.body: Every icon page now carries Add to cart beside Buy now. The cart lives on your device, shows a running count on its tab, lets you adjust quantities, and checks out everything in one payment with one shipping charge. Purify Plus members still ship free on every order.

sections.heading: Orders that tell the truth
sections.body: Starting a checkout and then walking away used to leave a phantom order marked as confirmed. No more. Backing out of the payment page cancels the attempt on the spot, unfinished checkouts appear only as a quiet removable note, never among your real orders, and anything unpaid says plainly: Awaiting Payment.

sections.heading: Icon pages on desktop, mended
sections.body: Opening an icon or the EIKON storefront on the desktop website could answer with an internal server error. The root cause is fixed and every shop page opens cleanly on every screen.

sections.heading: A proper amen to your payment
sections.body: When your payment goes through, a gold ring now draws its check, and the confirmation rises beneath it. Small, quick, and honored if your device asks for reduced motion.

sections.heading: Faster, calmer surfaces
sections.body: Shop pages now load with quiet placeholder cards instead of a bare loading line, browsing back and forth is instant, messages show who is speaking with the composer always in reach, and the browser tab reads cleanly on every shop page.

sections.heading: Account, always reachable
sections.body: On desktop, the account page could sit on a loading skeleton if the redirect script never woke. The skeleton now carries a plain link to your profile that works even with no script at all.

closing: Found within hours, mended within hours. If anything else is loose, write to lifeistheosis@gmail.com. I read every email, and I pray for the people who send them.

title: The Fathers, doubled: the whole Psalter with Augustine
intro: Welcome, and glory to Jesus Christ. This patch is one thing only, and it is a large thing: commentary. A reader on the Discord asked for more of the Fathers, enough to stand beside any catena Bible, and this is the answer. The library of patristic commentary in Purify roughly doubles today, to four thousand four hundred and eighty-one verse-notes across twenty-three books of Scripture, from fifteen Fathers of the Church. Every word of it is the Fathers' own, from named public-domain translations, and we tell you exactly which. The core of Purify stays free, today and always.

sections.heading: The whole Psalter, with St. Augustine
sections.body: The crown of this patch. St. Augustine's Expositions on the Book of Psalms now stands beside every one of the hundred and fifty psalms, one thousand eight hundred and ninety-eight notes keyed verse by verse. Open any psalm, tap a red-dotted verse, and Augustine prays it with you. Because Purify's Psalter is the Septuagint and Augustine preached from it too, his psalm often meets yours word for word. From the Nicene and Post-Nicene Fathers, volume eight.

sections.heading: The six days, with St. Basil
sections.body: St. Basil the Great's nine homilies of the Hexaemeron, the Church's great preaching on the days of creation, now stand in Genesis 1 in full, each homily set on the verse whose command it opens with. In the beginning God made the heaven and the earth; Basil takes it from there.

sections.heading: A second voice on the Gospel of John
sections.body: St. Augustine's one hundred and twenty-four Tractates on the Gospel of John now read alongside St. John Chrysostom's eighty-eight homilies, two Fathers on one Gospel, across all twenty-one chapters. Where they stand on the same verse, you read them together.

sections.heading: Revelation, opened
sections.body: The Apocalypse receives its first commentary in Purify: St. Victorinus of Pettau, bishop and martyr of the Diocletianic persecution, whose commentary on Revelation is the earliest that survives from the whole Church. Eighty-eight notes across nineteen chapters, from the Ante-Nicene Fathers, volume seven.

sections.heading: The first verse, reachable
sections.body: Commentary on a chapter's opening verse was hidden on phones: the illuminated drop cap left no room for the red marker, and the long-press menu pointed at a desktop-only panel. The opening verse now carries its marker after the text, and the menu opens the commentary sheet properly. Genesis 1:1, John 1:1, and every psalm's opening are reachable with a tap.

sections.heading: On languages, honestly
sections.body: The same reader asked for commentary in the app's other languages. The Fathers here are public-domain English translations, named on every note, and we will not run them through a machine and call it a translation. Faithful editions in other languages are future work, done properly or not at all.

closing: Asked for on the Discord, and answered with the biggest single addition of the Fathers Purify has ever shipped. If a note sits on the wrong verse or a word looks wrong, write to lifeistheosis@gmail.com; every citation names its source so you can check us. I read every email, and I pray for the people who send them.

title: The shop comes inside
intro: Welcome, and glory to Jesus Christ. Until now the EIKON shop opened in your phone's browser, a door that led out of the app. This patch brings the whole shop inside: a Shop tab on the bottom bar, every icon browsable and buyable without leaving Purify or signing in again, checkout completed in the app, and your orders and your messages to the seller waiting when you return. And a first for EIKON: reviews you can trust, left only by people who actually bought the item, with a plain count of how many have sold. The core of Purify stays free, today and always.

sections.heading: The shop, inside the app
sections.body: The marketplace now lives in Purify itself, not a browser window. A new Shop tab sits on the bottom bar beside Today, the Bible, Discover, and Prayers. Browse the icons, open a listing, read the details, and buy, all without leaving the app and without signing in a second time. Your orders and your conversations with the seller are there when you come back.

sections.heading: Checkout, without leaving
sections.body: Buying an icon now happens in the app. You tap Buy, the secure Stripe page opens over the app to take the card, and when it closes you land back on your orders, where the new order appears and moves from confirmed to shipped. Purify Plus members still ship free on every order.

sections.heading: Reviews you can trust
sections.body: Every icon and every store can now carry a star rating, and a review can be left only by someone who actually bought the item, so no rating is idle talk. Each listing shows its average stars, how many reviews it has, and a plain count of how many have sold. Where nothing has sold or been reviewed yet, nothing is shown; we would rather say little than pad it out.

sections.heading: Message the seller, reach your requests
sections.body: Now that the shop is inside the app, messaging the seller and tracking an Icon Request work from your pocket the same as on the web. Ask about an order, request a saint the catalog does not hold yet, and read the replies, all in one place.

closing: The shop was the last room of Purify that still opened outward; now every room is under one roof. If anything is loose, write to lifeistheosis@gmail.com. I read every email, and I pray for the people who send them.

title: The account pages, mended
intro: Welcome, and glory to Jesus Christ. A quick repair patch for three crashes the first users found on the app: the account pages, the Purify Plus screen, and a top bar that slipped under the clock in the reader. All three are mended. The core of Purify stays free, today and always.

sections.heading: Your account, reachable again
sections.body: On the app, opening Account and security, or Notifications, was bouncing you back to sign-in or closing the screen. The offline app checks who you are the wrong way on those pages; it now checks the right way, so your profile, security, notification, and session settings all open as they should, without signing you out.

sections.heading: Purify Plus opens cleanly

sections.heading: The top bar clears the clock
